 Hearn Wants Mayweather to Risk 50–0 Against Garcia
 Google News Preferred Source 
 By Tom Galm - 11/17/2026 - Comments 
 Eddie Hearn wants Floyd Mayweather Jr. to end his exhibition run and put his 50 and 0 record on the line against reigning world champion Ryan Garcia. In an interview this week, Hearn compared the idea of Mayweather returning to face an active titleholder to George Foreman winning the heavyweight crown back in the nineties.
 Hearn views it as an exciting idea, yet notice who he is leaving out of the conversation. Hearn promotes unified junior middleweight champion Jaron Ennis, and he is certainly not pushing Mayweather to step into that human guillotine. Even though casual fans would pay big money hoping to see Mayweather finally get flattened, matching a guy turning 50 in February 2027 against Ennis would look like a sanctioned mugging rather than a sporting event.
 Ryan Garcia is a completely different story. Despite holding a world title, Ryan has looked vulnerable whenever an opponent survives his early power and takes away his leaping left hook. His clear loss to Rolly Romero exposed how quickly he runs out of ideas when he has to lead, and even when he dropped Devin Haney badly in 2024, he got wild and could not finish the job.
 If Ryan were a relentless volume puncher with power, a 49-year-old Mayweather would be in huge trouble. Even in his mid-thirties back in 2014, Mayweather got smothered against the ropes and took heavy shots in two close fights against Marcos Maidana because he could not dodge nonstop punches from every angle. Ryan is a single-shot hunter who needs space to set up his left hook, giving Mayweather plenty of breathing room to use his upper body slip, low crouch, and stiff jab to steal quiet rounds on the outside.
 “If you want to come back, fight the reigning world champion, someone like Ryan Garcia,” said Hearn on the Mr. Versace podcast. “I think that’s a thrilling narrative and storyline. I mean, it’s like Foreman coming back, isn’t it?
 “That’s, for me, that’s worse than losing your O,” Hearn said of the exhibition run.
 For Mayweather, trading his unbeaten record for one last monster payday makes total sense if the rumors about his cash crunch are true. You cannot spend an undefeated record, and if he loses at 50, nobody holds it against him anyway.
 Ryan is the one walking into a career-risk situation. If he loses to a 50-year-old retiree, that embarrassment follows him forever, and it is tough to see him having the thick skin to brush off that kind of permanent stain.
